_comment: THE SECOND CALIBRATION CASE, and the one backlog p5-16 asked for: a career
base that GENUINELY COVERS most of its vacancy. Every number this project has
measured about grounding came from the sibling fixture
calibration-case-hiredbuddy.json, whose base deliberately does NOT cover the
posting - so nothing there could separate 'the generator over-claims' from
'the corpus is thin'. This case is the control for that confound.
BOTH PEOPLE AND BOTH COMPANIES ARE INVENTED. Kai Lindqvist, Falkenberg
Analytics, Nordhavn Retail Group and Vinterlys Data GmbH do not exist; the
posting is written here rather than copied, for the reason the sibling
fixtures give - a verbatim third-party posting is someone else's copy in this
repository. Every address in it is on example.com, which is reserved for
documentation and can never reach a real inbox.
WHY DATA ENGINEERING. Rule B1's lexical evidence gate only fires on
requirements P1 classifies as `tool` or `credential`, so demonstrating it
needs a role whose postings are dense with named products. Data-engineering
postings are almost entirely named tools, which makes this the case where the
gate has the most to decide. It is also the furthest from the existing
AI-quality/annotation persona, so the second fixture is a different corpus
rather than a variation on the first.
WHAT IT IS BUILT TO PRODUCE, and the design is the point rather than the
outcome:
- SIX named tools appear literally in BOTH texts - Python, SQL, Airflow,
dbt, Snowflake, Docker - so those requirements should clear the gate and
read Covered. That is what the first fixture never had.
- THREE named tools appear in the posting and NOWHERE in the base - Kafka,
Terraform, and Spark/Databricks - so those should read Gap.
- The base does ADJACENT work for all three, deliberately: 'checkout event
topics' beside Kafka, 'infrastructure-as-code modules' beside Terraform,
'partitioned Parquet' beside Spark. That is what makes them a test of the
GATE rather than of the threshold: topical similarity should be high
enough to clear 0.36, and the gate should refuse them anyway because the
base never names the thing. A row that fails on similarity alone proves
nothing about the gate.
- Two or three requirements are therefore genuinely uncovered. A case where
everything is Covered would teach a reader nothing and would not be a
calibration case at all.
Seed it the way the sibling fixtures are seeded, or through
scripts/demo-seed.mjs, which drives the same flows as a signed-in user and
captures the README screenshots from the result.
Findings live in docs/eval/generation-coverage-control.md.
resumeText:
KAI LINDQVIST
Data Engineer — Munich, Germany

SUMMARY
Four years building batch and near-real-time data pipelines for analytics
teams: Airflow orchestration, dbt transformations on Snowflake, and the Python
and SQL around both.

EXPERIENCE

Data Engineer — Falkenberg Analytics (03/2024 – present)
Owned 40 production Airflow DAGs moving roughly 2 TB per day from operational
Postgres databases and partner APIs into Snowflake, and cut the nightly critical
path from 5 h 10 m to 2 h 45 m by rewriting the two widest joins as incremental
models.
Built the dbt project the analytics team works in: 180 models, source freshness
tests on every ingestion table, and a CI job that runs the full dbt build against
a Snowflake clone on every pull request.
Wrote the Python ingestion framework that pulls from partner APIs with retries,
schema validation and dead-letter storage, and made schema drift a build failure
instead of a Monday morning surprise.
Carried the on-call pager for the platform one week in four and reduced pipeline
pages by 60 percent over two quarters by adding freshness alerts and idempotent
retries.

Analytics Engineer — Nordhavn Retail Group (06/2022 – 02/2024)
Modelled the sales and inventory marts as a star schema with slowly changing
dimensions, replacing 900 lines of hand-written SQL views with tested dbt models
the finance team could read for themselves.
Built streaming ingestion from the checkout event topics into a near-real-time
inventory table, with late-arriving events handled by a windowed merge.
Containerised the transformation stack with Docker so a new analyst could run the
whole pipeline locally with one command, and wired that image into the CI
pipeline that gates every merge.
Provisioned the warehouse, its roles and its access policies as
infrastructure-as-code modules reviewed in pull requests rather than clicked in a
console.

Junior Data Analyst — Nordhavn Retail Group (09/2021 – 05/2022)
Wrote the SQL behind the weekly trading pack and automated its distribution.
Rebuilt three recurring analyses as partitioned Parquet extracts, cutting the
report refresh from 40 minutes to under 4.

SKILLS
Python (pandas, SQLAlchemy), SQL, Apache Airflow, dbt, Snowflake, PostgreSQL,
Docker, CI pipelines, data modelling, star schemas, slowly changing dimensions,
dimensional warehouse design, Parquet, near-real-time ingestion. English C1,
Swedish native, German B1.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science — Lunds universitet (2018 – 2021)
vacancyText:
Data Engineer — Vinterlys Data GmbH, Munich (hybrid, two days on site)

Vinterlys Data builds the reporting platform used by mid-sized European
retailers. We are hiring a Data Engineer to join the four-person platform team
that owns ingestion, transformation and the warehouse everything else reads
from.

What you will do:
- Build and maintain the production pipelines that land partner and operational
  data in our warehouse, and own them once they are live.
- Model the data the analytics team consumes, and keep the tests that stop a bad
  load reaching a dashboard.
- Take part in the on-call rotation for the platform, one week in four.
- Review your team-mates' pipeline changes and have your own reviewed.

What we are looking for:
- 3+ years building and maintaining production data pipelines.
- Strong SQL and solid Python.
- Production experience with Apache Airflow.
- Hands-on experience with dbt for transformation and testing.
- Experience with a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake or BigQuery.
- Experience with streaming data using Apache Kafka.
- Working knowledge of Terraform for infrastructure as code.
- Comfortable with Docker and a CI pipeline.
- Solid data modelling: star schemas, slowly changing dimensions, and knowing
  when not to normalise.
- Good written English; German is useful but not required.

Nice to have:
- Experience with Apache Spark or Databricks for large batch workloads.
- Exposure to schema-drift detection or data contracts.

We offer a permanent contract, 30 days of holiday, a hybrid setup in Munich and
a yearly training budget.
